articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entity in North Korea IT Worker Schemes, DRC-Related Actions
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) on October 28, 2026, sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their involvement in North Korean government-run IT worker schemes. These schemes generate significant revenue for the DPRK's weapons programs by defrauding U.S. businesses through fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and fabricated personas.

The action targets key facilitators and financial networks that sustain these illicit schemes, with the DPRK regime appropriating most of the workers' wages to fund its unlawful weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs.
Additionally, OFAC announced designations related to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, further expanding its efforts to counter illicit activities globally.

articles.headline: OFAC Reaches Settlement Agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc.

Details of the settlement, including the specific violations and the agreed-upon penalty, are available through OFAC's official channels.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026.
These amendments pertain to guidance regarding blocking and rejecting transactions, as well as filing reports with OFAC, as part of an ongoing review process to ensure information remains current.
The updated FAQs (10, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53) provide clarifications and updates for financial institutions and other entities subject to OFAC regulations.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' targeting Iran's shadow fleet network.

These actions targeted a network of legal, maritime, and shipping service providers, including a Panama- and Greece-based law firm, shipping agents, and cargo vessels, for facilitating Iran's sanctions evasion and petroleum trade.

In a separate action, OFAC also announced the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea, alongside the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Legal 500 / ABA Banking Journal / VOA Editorials

These designations target individuals and entities involved in illicit drug trafficking and terrorist financing activities, aiming to disrupt their financial networks.
The actions underscore the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to combating global illicit finance and national security threats.

articles.headline: EU Imposes Largest-Ever Single Round of Russia Sanctions, Targeting Military-Industrial Complex
body: The European Union adopted its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia on October 12, 2026, marking its largest-ever single round of listings.
This unprecedented action added 1,569 companies and executives to its restrictive measures list, specifically targeting Russia's military-industrial complex and its broader industrial supply chains.

The new designations include 826 companies and 743 executives involved in the production and supply of components for missiles, drones, and military aircraft, bringing the total number of listings under the EU's Ukraine-related sanctions regime to nearly 4,600.

articles.headline: UK Expands Russia Sanctions Targeting Energy, Shipping, and Military Supply Chains
body: The United Kingdom expanded its sanctions against Russia on October 8, 2026, with a package comprising 38 new designations.

These measures specifically targeted Russian oil companies, shadow fleet tankers, payment platforms, crypto-exchanges, and entities involved in the procurement, manufacture, and transport of goods supporting Russia's military-industrial base.
This action demonstrates the UK's continued focus on disrupting Russia's energy revenues, sanctions circumvention networks, and shadow fleet activities.

body: The Nasdaq Composite experienced a 1.4% decline on October 29, 2026, primarily driven by a significant drop in Alphabet's stock.

articles.headline: Euro Area Inflation Rises to 3.8% in September, ECB Keeps Rates Unchanged
body: Inflation in the euro area rose to 3.8% in September, up from 3.2% in August, according to the European Central Bank (ECB).

Despite the rising inflation, the ECB's Governing Council decided on October 29, 2026, to keep the three key ECB interest rates unchanged, citing continued increases in energy prices as posing upside risks to the inflation outlook and downside risks to growth.
The ECB remains committed to its 2% medium-term inflation target and will continue to follow a data-dependent approach to monetary policy.

articles.headline: Federal Reserve Maintains Interest Rates; Two Officials Dissent for Rate Hike
body: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent on October 28, 2026.
This decision comes after a rate hike in September, with the Committee noting that economic activity is expanding at a strong pace, but inflation remains elevated.
Two officials, Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, preferring a quarter-point rate hike at this meeting.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for October 2026, Including $750 Million Penalty Against Bank of America
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released its enforcement actions for October 2026, detailing various penalties against financial institutions.

A significant action includes a Cease and Desist Order and a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, Sandy, Utah, for deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act compliance program, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and customer due diligence and customer identification program violations.

The OCC also issued Orders of Prohibition against Jennifer Hamblin, a Vault Teller at Fifth Third Bank, N.A., and Christopher Organista, a Former Operations Processor at U.S. Bank National Association, for embezzling customer and bank funds, respectively.

articles.headline: OCC Releases Report on 'Debanking' Practices at Largest National Banks
body: On October 14, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released 'Guaranteeing Fair Banking for All Americans,' a report presenting the findings of its supervisory review of 'debanking' practices at the nine largest national banks it supervises.

The OCC concluded that during the period from September 2020 through September 2025, each of the nine banks maintained reputation risk and industry-specific policies, practices, and procedures that lacked sufficiently clear standards and objective, risk-based criteria.

The report suggests these policies presented an elevated risk of denying access to financial services and disadvantaged certain Americans based on their political, religious, or social views or lawful business activities.

articles.headline: DHS Adds Three Chinese Genomics Companies to UFLPA Entity List Over Forced Labor Allegations
body: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), on behalf of the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force (FLETF), announced the addition of three Chinese companies to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List, effective October 29, 2026.

The three affiliated companies, Shenzhen BGI Technology Co., Ltd. (BGI Group), BGI Genomics Co., Ltd., and MGI Tech Co., Ltd., are accused of involvement in the government's testing of minorities in the Xinjiang region and helping to build and operate its mass surveillance infrastructure.

This action means goods made by these companies are prohibited from entering the United States unless the importer can demonstrate they were not made with forced labor, further expanding the UFLPA Entity List to 190 entities.

articles.headline: Revisions to the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing one entity from the Entity List under the destination of Turkey.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
